messages.cron.editUnsupported:
crontab -e opens your crontab in a text editor, which the simulator does not have yet.
Write the jobs in a file and install it with  crontab FILE , or add a line with:
  (crontab -l; echo '*/5 * * * * date >> ~/cron.log') | crontab -
messages.disks.formatPartitionsOnly: The simulator only formats partitions (e.g. /dev/sdb1), not whole disks.
messages.disks.noPartitionChanges: The simulator does not pretend to change partition tables – this is where you can really destroy a disk. Use fdisk -l to look.
messages.disks.shellInsideDir: Simulator tip: your shell is inside the directory. Leave it first, e.g. with cd ~.
messages.disks.wholeDiskTip: Simulator tip: {disk} is the whole disk. The file system is on a partition – try {disk}{suffix}.
messages.extras.editorUnsupported:
{editor} is an interactive text editor and is not supported in the simulator yet.
Create files with e.g.  echo 'text' > file.txt  or  echo 'more text' >> file.txt
messages.extras.htopSnapshot: (Simulated snapshot. In a real terminal htop is interactive – quit with q.)
messages.extras.pythonInteractive: Python {version} – interactive mode is not supported in the simulator yet.
messages.fish.bashSyntax: That is bash syntax. In fish, if, for, while and function blocks are closed with "end" – no then, do, done or fi.
messages.git.commitNoEditor: (Real git now opens a text editor for the commit message. The simulator has none – give the message directly: git commit -m "What the change does")
messages.git.configEditUnsupported: (The simulator has no editor for git config -e. Use git config <key> <value>, or change the file with e.g. echo.)
messages.git.manGitHint: (Type man git for the simulator's manual page about git.)
messages.git.manGitOptions: (See man git for the options the simulator supports.)
messages.git.mergeMsgUsed: (The simulator has no editor, so the suggested message from .git/MERGE_MSG is used.)
messages.git.mergeSquashUnsupported: (git merge --squash is not supported in the simulator.)
messages.git.noNetwork: (The simulator has no network, so git {action} cannot reach {host}. It does work with repositories on this computer, e.g. git clone ~/projekt-webb ~/kopia.)
messages.git.octopusUnsupported: (Merging several branches at once (octopus) is not supported in the simulator.)
messages.git.pullRebaseUnsupported: (git pull --rebase is not supported in the simulator – run git pull without --rebase.)
messages.git.reflogShowOnly: (Only git reflog [show] is supported in the simulator.)
messages.git.shellAliasUnsupported: (Aliases that run shell commands (!) are not supported in the simulator.)
messages.git.tagNoEditor: (The simulator has no editor. Give the message with -m "…".)
messages.net.addressChangeUnsupported: (Changing addresses is not supported in the simulator.)
messages.net.curlRedirect: (The server answered {status} {reason} – the page has moved to {location}. Add -L to make curl follow it.)
messages.net.myserverBackground: (myserver now runs in the background. Try  curl http://localhost:{port}  – and stop it with  pkill myserver)
messages.net.nslookupInteractive: (Interactive mode is not supported in the simulator. Type e.g.  nslookup example.com)
messages.net.pingCtrlC: (In a real terminal ping keeps going until you press Ctrl+C. With -c 4 only four packets are sent.)
messages.net.routeChangeUnsupported: (Changing routes is not supported in the simulator.)
messages.net.ssNoConnections: (No open connections right now. Add -l to see listening ports, e.g. "ss -tulpn".)
messages.net.ssProcessColumn: (The process column is empty for processes owned by other users. Run "sudo ss -tulpn" to see all of them.)
messages.pkg.aptListsEmpty: Tip from the simulator: the package lists are empty. Run 'sudo apt update' first.
messages.pkg.aptUpgradeNeedsUpdate: Tip from the simulator: apt doesn't know about any new versions until you have run 'sudo apt update'.
messages.pkg.essentialPackage: {pkg} is an essential package – without it the system stops working.
messages.pkg.onlyInAur: Simulator tip: {pkg} is not in the Arch repositories, only in the AUR (see the chapter "AUR, PPA and COPR").
messages.procs.fgJobDone: The simulator doesn't wait – the job counts as done.
messages.procs.killOwnShell: The simulator won't let you kill your own shell.
messages.procs.topSnapshot: Snapshot. In a real terminal top updates continuously – quit with q.
messages.repos.emptyDirectory: (The directory is empty - maybe there was no AUR package with that name?)
messages.repos.goSubcommandUnsupported: go {subcommand} is not supported in the simulator.
messages.repos.installBaseDevel: Simulator tip: install the build tools first: sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel
messages.repos.makepkgNoSudo: Simulator tip: run makepkg without sudo. It uses sudo by itself when the package is installed.
messages.repos.makepkgSyncDeps: Simulator tip: with -s makepkg installs the dependencies for you (makepkg -si).
messages.repos.noSuchAurPackage: (There is no AUR package called "{name}". Check the name on aur.archlinux.org or with "yay -Ss".)
messages.repos.onlyPretendAur: (The simulator can only build the packages in its pretend AUR.)
messages.repos.ppaFormat: Simulator tip: a PPA is written ppa:user/name, e.g. ppa:lunatool/moonphase.
messages.repos.ppaWarning: Simulator warning: PPAs are built for Ubuntu (here {suite}), not for {distro}. The packages may need other library versions than Debian has and can break the system.
messages.repos.snowQuit: (In a real terminal the snow keeps falling until you press q.)
messages.repos.ubuntuOnlyComponent: (The {component} component only exists in Ubuntu - Debian has main, contrib and non-free.)
messages.repos.yayPkgbuildHint: (yay shows the PKGBUILD files here if you want to read them - they are in ~/.cache/yay/.)
messages.run.watchOnce: (watch runs the command again every {seconds} s until you press Ctrl+C – the simulator shows it once.)
messages.scp.oneSide: (In the simulator scp copies between this computer and the server: put HOST: on the sources or on the target, not on both.)
messages.script.readInScripts: In the simulator, read inside a script can only read from a pipe or a file, e.g. "echo text | ./script.sh".
messages.shell.commandInPackage: Tip from the simulator: the command is in the package '{pkg}'. See the chapter on package management.
messages.shell.exitNoSession: This is a simulated terminal, so there is no session to end. Use 'clear' to clear the screen.
messages.shell.stepLimit: The simulator stopped the run after {steps} steps – an infinite loop, perhaps? (In a real terminal you stop a program that never finishes with Ctrl+C.)
messages.shell.welcome:
Simulated terminal ({distro}). Nothing you do here affects your computer.
Type 'help' to see which commands are available.
messages.shellmode.zshMainMenu: The main menu is not available in the simulator – you get the recommended settings (as with 2).
messages.shells.loginShellChanged: The login shell for {user} is now {shell} (see /etc/passwd). It takes effect at the next login – the terminal you have open still runs its old shell.
messages.ssh.noInteractiveShell: (The simulator can't give you an interactive shell on the server. Put the command right after the host, e.g.  ssh {dest} 'ls -l')
messages.ssh.onlyServer: (In the simulator you can only log in to server.lan, 192.168.1.10.)
messages.ssh.ownComputerOnlyServer: (This is your own computer – sshd is listening, but in the simulator you can only log in to server.lan, 192.168.1.10.)
messages.system.alreadyBash: You're already running bash! The simulator can't start a new interactive shell.
messages.system.helpManHint: Type 'man <command>' for more information about a command.
messages.system.helpMissingProgram: Missing a program? Maybe you can install it with the package manager ({pm}).
messages.system.manScrollHint: In a real terminal you scroll through the manual with the arrow keys and quit with q.
messages.system.suRootNoPassword: Tip: the root account has no password here, so su won't work. Use 'sudo -i' instead.
messages.system.suUserNoPassword: Tip: {user} has no password or is locked. Set one with 'sudo passwd {user}' – or use 'sudo -iu {user}'.
messages.system.sudoAdminGroup: Tip: only members of the {group} group may use sudo.
messages.systemd.cannotPowerOff: (The simulator can't be powered off – try sudo systemctl reboot instead.)
messages.systemd.hostnameSaved: (The name is saved in /etc/hostname. In the simulator the prompt still shows the old name.)
messages.systemd.journalFollow: (journalctl -f keeps showing new lines until you press Ctrl+C. The simulator only shows the latest lines.)
messages.systemd.needsRoot: (Changing services requires root – put sudo in front of the command.)
messages.systemd.noUserServices: (The simulator only has system services – skip --user.)
messages.systemd.rebooted: (The computer reboots … done! You're logged in as {user} again. See what happened with journalctl -b -1 (previous boot) and journalctl -b.)
messages.text.tailFollow: simulator: -f doesn't follow the file – in a real terminal you stop it with Ctrl+C
messages.textproc.awkNote: only part of awk is available here: patterns, BEGIN/END, fields, variables, arrays, if/while/for, print, printf and the most common functions. See `man awk`.
messages.textproc.awkTooManySteps: the program was stopped after too many steps – an infinite loop, perhaps?
messages.textproc.sedUnsupported: the sed command {command} is not supported here – only s, d, p, q, Q, y, =, a, i and c. See `man sed`.
messages.universal.addRemoteFirst: Simulator tip: add the remote first: flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flathub {url}
messages.universal.appImageFuse: Simulator tip: install the FUSE 2 library - on {distro} the package is called {pkg}. Or run it with --appimage-extract-and-run.
messages.universal.flatpakPolkit: (Without sudo, Flatpak asks for your password in a window (polkit). The simulator skips that.)
messages.universal.graphicalApp: ({app} is a graphical program and would now open in a window of its own. The simulator only has a terminal, so this is where it stops.)
messages.universal.noRemotes: Simulator tip: you have no remotes yet. Add Flathub with flatpak remote-add.
messages.universal.remoteSystemOnly: ({remote} only exists in the system installation. The user installation has its own remotes - add it with --user.)
messages.universal.snapPathAdded: (/snap/bin was added to PATH. On a real system that happens the next time you log in.)
messages.universal.unusedRuntimes: Tip: the runtimes are still there. Remove those no app uses with: flatpak uninstall --unused
messages.users.chfnSkips: (The simulator skips room number, phone numbers and "Other".)
messages.users.lowercaseNames: Tip: user names use lowercase letters a–z.
messages.users.needsRoot: Tip: this needs root – try putting sudo in front.
messages.users.noPasswordSet: No password was set. Set it later with: sudo passwd {user}
messages.users.passwordHidden: What you type isn't shown – just like in a real terminal. Type the password and press Enter.
messages.users.skipsCurrentPassword: (Current password: – the simulator skips your current password)
